examples.en: He spoke in a joking tone, but his eyes were serious.
I was misunderstood because of my joking way of speaking.
Everyone laughed at the answer with a joking tone mixed in.
It was in a joking tone, so I can't tell if he meant it.

examples.ko: 그렇게 농담조로 넘기지 말고 제대로 대답해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't brush it off as a joke like that; please answer properly.
My friend sent a letter written in a joking tone, and I laughed.

explain: '-조'는 말투나 느낌을 나타내는 말이에요. '명령조', '비난조'처럼 쓰이고, 농담조는 '농담조로 말하다'가 가장 흔해요. '농담처럼'과 비슷하지만 말투 자체가 장난스러울 때 써요.

phrases.en: He spoke in a joking tone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 말하는 방식을 나타내는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, with '로' marking the manner of speaking.

phrases.en: His joking tone of voice made me feel bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '의' is added to modify the following noun.

phrases.en: I said it like a joke, but I meant it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농담조'와 비슷하지만 말투보다 내용이 농담 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '농담조', but used when the content, rather than the tone, seems like a joke.

explain_en: The suffix '-조' marks a tone or manner of speaking, as in '명령조' (commanding tone) and '비난조' (accusing tone). 농담조 is most often used as '농담조로 말하다'. It is close to '농담처럼' (like a joke), but fits when the way of speaking itself is playful.

examples.en: Birds fly freely through the sky.

examples.ko: 이 도서관에서는 책을 자유로이 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this library you can read books freely.
He expressed his thoughts freely.
The kids run and play freely on the playground.
I want to use my time freely.

examples.ko: 누구나 자유로이 의견을 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can freely offer an opinion.

explain: 말할 때는 '자유롭게'가 훨씬 흔하고, '자유로이'는 글 같은 느낌이 조금 있어요. 둘 다 '자유롭다'에서 온 부사예요. ㅂ 불규칙 형용사라서 '자유롭다'가 '자유로이'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: Please sit freely here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같고 말할 때 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more common in speech.

phrases.en: People of the two countries come and go freely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오가거나 드나드는 일이 막히지 않을 때 글 같은 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a written tone when coming and going is unrestricted.

phrases.en: I played to my heart's content in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 만큼 한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses doing something as much as you like.

explain_en: In speech '자유롭게' is much more common, while '자유로이' sounds a bit written. Both are adverbs from '자유롭다'. Because it is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, '자유롭다' turns into '자유로이'.

en: to be reasonable; to be logical

examples.ko: 부장님 말씀이 지당하다고 모두 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: Everyone nodded, saying the manager's words were absolutely right.
It's absolutely true that health is the most important thing.
Getting angry is a perfectly natural reaction.
That's quite right, but it's hard to do right away.

examples.ko: 그렇게 하라는 충고가 지당해서 반박을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The advice to do so was so right that I couldn't argue back.

examples.ko: 그의 의견은 지당하지만 지금 상황에는 맞지 않아요.
examples.en: His opinion is quite right, but it doesn't suit the current situation.

explain: '지당한 말씀'처럼 말이나 의견에 잘 어울려요. 윗사람의 말에 '맞는 말씀이에요'라고 높여 대답할 때 쓰지만, 말투에 따라 뻔한 소리라고 비꼬는 느낌이 될 수도 있어요. '당연하다'보다 격식 있는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Teacher, what you say is perfectly right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람의 말에 높여서 맞다고 대답할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely agree with something a superior has said.
phrases.en_equiv: What you say is quite right

phrases.example: 열심히 한 사람이 상을 받는 것은 지당한 일이에요.
phrases.en: It is only right that the person who worked hard receives the prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마땅하고 당연한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things that are proper and only natural.

phrases.en: I also think that remark is quite right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 의견이 옳다고 생각한다는 뜻을 격식 있게 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat formal way of saying you think an opinion is correct.
phrases.en_equiv: to think it is quite right

explain_en: It fits words and opinions, as in '지당한 말씀' (a perfectly right remark). It can show respect when agreeing with a superior, but depending on tone it can also sound sarcastic, as if saying 'that's obvious'. It feels more formal than '당연하다'.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 확실성이 낮아서 더 알아봐야 해요.
examples.en: This plan has low certainty, so we need to look into it more.

examples.ko: 결과의 확실성을 높이려면 실험을 여러 번 해야 해요.
examples.en: To raise the certainty of the result, you have to run the experiment several times.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 믿기 전에 정보의 확실성부터 확인해요.
examples.en: Before believing the news, I first check how reliable the information is.

examples.ko: 그 소문은 확실성이 없어서 말하기 조심스러워요.
examples.en: That rumor isn't certain, so I'm careful about repeating it.

examples.ko: 때로는 확실성보다 속도가 더 중요한 일도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes speed matters more than certainty.

examples.ko: 투자할 때는 수익의 확실성을 꼭 따져 봐요.
examples.en: When investing, I always weigh how certain the profit is.

explain: 일상에서는 '확실하다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '확실성'은 설명문이나 뉴스, 발표에서 자주 나와요. 반대말 '불확실성'은 경제 뉴스에서 특히 자주 들려요. '확실성이 높다/낮다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 소문은 확실성이 없어서 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: That rumor isn't certain, so it's hard to believe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿을 만한 근거가 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is no reliable basis.

phrases.example: 확인을 한 번 더 해서 확실성을 높였어요.
phrases.en: I checked once more to raise the certainty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높이다'와 함께 더 믿을 수 있게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 'nopida', it means making something more reliable.

phrases.en: These days economic uncertainty is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말로, 경제 뉴스에서 특히 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite word, especially common in economic news.

explain_en: In daily talk '확실하다' is more common, while '확실성' appears in explanations, news and presentations. Its opposite '불확실성' is heard especially often in economic news. People say '확실성이 높다/낮다'.

en: to be smart; to be bright

examples.en: That child is young but really bright.
A sharp junior joined, so I feel reassured.
It was a child with bright-looking eyes.
I'm raising a smart-looking puppy.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 똘똘해서 말을 빨리 배웠어요.
examples.en: My daughter is bright and learned to talk early.
Class is fun thanks to a bright student.

explain: 주로 어린아이나 젊은 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 아랫사람을 보는 느낌이 들 수 있어서 '똑똑하다'가 더 안전해요. '똑똑하다'보다 야무지고 귀여운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: A bright child lives next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 어린아이를 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often praises a child by modifying a noun.

phrases.example: 그 학생은 눈이 반짝여서 똘똘해 보여요.
phrases.en: That student looks bright with sparkling eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습으로 느끼는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an impression based on looks.

phrases.en: The teacher is really smart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게도 쓸 수 있는 더 안전한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A safer word that can be used for adults too.

explain_en: It is mainly used to praise children or young people. Used on an adult it can sound condescending, so '똑똑하다' is safer. It feels more sharp-and-cute than '똑똑하다'.

examples.en: Talking loudly on the phone in a movie theater is really rude and thoughtless.

examples.ko: 줄을 서지 않고 새치기하는 건 몰상식한 행동이에요.
examples.en: Cutting in line is senseless, rude behavior.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말이 너무 몰상식해서 대화하기 싫어요.
examples.en: He speaks so rudely that I don't want to talk to him.

examples.ko: 몰상식하게 쓰레기를 길에 버리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't throw trash on the street so thoughtlessly.
I was careful because I didn't want to be called rude.

examples.ko: 어른께 그렇게 말하는 건 좀 몰상식하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it a bit out of line to speak to an elder like that?

explain: 예의나 기본 상식이 없는 행동을 비난할 때 써서 꽤 강한 말이에요. 사람에게 직접 말하기보다 행동을 두고 '몰상식한 행동'처럼 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '예의가 없다', '개념이 없다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A person with no common sense upset me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 없는 사람을 비난할 때 쓰지만 강한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a rude person, but it's a strong expression.

phrases.en: I saw someone behaving without any common sense on the bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 행동을 꾸밀 때 써요. 비난하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게 it describes how someone acts; it carries strong criticism.

phrases.en: Talking loudly on the phone in a theater shows no sense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '몰상식하다' 대신 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday alternative to 몰상식하다.

explain_en: It criticizes behavior that lacks basic manners or sense, so it is quite strong. People usually use it about an action, as in '몰상식한 행동', rather than say it directly to a person. In daily talk Koreans also say '예의가 없다' or '개념이 없다'.

examples.en: The defendant entered the court with his lawyer.
The defense counsel argued for innocence.

examples.ko: 경찰은 조사 전에 변호인을 부를 수 있다고 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The police said he could call counsel before questioning.
The defense side submitted new evidence.

examples.ko: 그는 믿을 만한 변호인을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is looking for a trustworthy lawyer.
I heard the defense counsel's statement on the news.

explain: 재판이나 수사에서 피고인 편에서 돕는 사람을 가리켜요. 일반적으로 법률 일을 하는 직업은 '변호사'라고 해요. 같은 사람이어도 사건 안에서의 역할을 말하면 '변호인', 직업을 말하면 '변호사'예요.

phrases.en: The defense side said the evidence was not enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재판 뉴스에서 피고인 쪽 사람들을 함께 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in trial news for the defendant's side as a whole.

phrases.en: A famous defense team took the case.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명이 함께 변호하는 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A team of several people defending together.

phrases.en: I want to become a lawyer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건 안의 역할이 아니라 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the profession rather than the role in a case.

explain_en: It refers to the person who stands with the accused during a trial or investigation. The profession is 변호사. The same person is 변호인 when you talk about the role in a case, and 변호사 when you talk about the job.

examples.en: It's really thoughtless of you to say that.
Thoughtless behavior makes things hard for everyone.
You're not a child, so why are you so thoughtless?
Everyone was shocked by his indiscreet words.
I apologize for my thoughtless behavior.
You end up regretting careless spending later.

explain: 앞뒤를 가리지 못하고 경솔하다는 뜻이라 사람이나 행동을 비판할 때 써요. '철없다'는 어린 느낌이 강하고, '분별없다'는 어른에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대는 '분별 있다'이고, 주로 '분별없는 행동/말'로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 분별없는 말 때문에 친구가 상처를 받았어요.
phrases.en: My friend was hurt by thoughtless words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각 없이 한 말을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize words said without thinking.

phrases.en: If you act recklessly, you will regret it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형 '분별없이'를 동사 앞에 붙인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form '분별없이' placed before a verb.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 분별없지 않아요. 늘 신중해요.
phrases.en: He is not indiscreet. He is always careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 신중하다는 뜻을 전할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can convey that someone is careful.

explain_en: It means being careless without thinking things through, so it is used to criticize a person or an action. '철없다' feels childish, while '분별없다' can be used for adults too. The opposite is '분별 있다', and it is mostly used as '분별없는 행동/말'.

en: to be upright; to be square; to be right-minded

examples.ko: 그분은 마음이 올곧아서 거짓말을 못 해요.
examples.en: He is so upright that he can't tell a lie.

examples.ko: 올곧은 성격 때문에 손해를 볼 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I lose out because of my upright character.
My teacher is someone who has lived an upright life.
He stayed upright against every temptation.

examples.ko: 올곧다는 평가를 받는 기자가 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: A reporter known as upright received an award.
I want to be an upright and warm person.

explain: 주로 사람의 마음, 태도, 삶이 바르고 곧을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. 활용은 '올곧아요, 올곧은, 올곧게'처럼 해요.

phrases.en: He is an upright person, so everyone trusts him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 '올곧은'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 올곧은 before a noun.

phrases.en: Our teacher is very upright at heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for giving praise.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived an upright life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삶의 태도를 말할 때 부사형 '올곧게'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form 올곧게 describes how one lives.

explain_en: It is mostly praise for a person's mind, attitude or way of life being right and straight. It conjugates as '올곧아요, 올곧은, 올곧게'.

examples.ko: 그 아저씨는 입심이 좋아서 늘 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That man is a great talker, so he's always popular.

examples.ko: 입심 좋은 사회자 덕분에 행사가 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the smooth-talking host, the event was fun.
Nobody can beat my grandmother's gift of gab.
Some broadcasters make a living with their way with words.

examples.ko: 그 가이드는 입심도 좋고 아는 것도 많아요.
examples.en: That guide talks well and also knows a lot.

examples.ko: 입심만 믿고 준비 없이 발표하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't present without preparing, relying only on your talking skills.

explain: 보통 '입심이 좋다', '입심이 세다'처럼 말해요. '입담', '말솜씨'와 비슷하게 쓰이는 구어적인 말이고, 말을 막힘없이 잘한다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 입심이 세서 아무도 못 이겨요.
phrases.en: Grandma is so quick-tongued that nobody can beat her in talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 지지 않고 막힘없이 잘한다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger sense of never losing in a verbal exchange and talking without pause.

phrases.example: 그는 입심 좋게 이야기를 풀어 갔어요.
phrases.en: He told the story with great fluency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 방식을 나타내는 부사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb describing the way someone speaks.
phrases.en_equiv: fluently; with a gift of gab

phrases.en: He's a good talker, so his stories are always fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입심과 비슷하지만 이야기를 재미있게 한다는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 입심, but with more emphasis on telling entertaining stories.

explain_en: It is usually said as '입심이 좋다' or '입심이 세다'. It is a colloquial word used much like '입담' or '말솜씨', and it suggests speaking fluently without hesitation.

examples.en: Please feel free to state your opinion in the meeting.

examples.ko: 그는 정책에 대한 반대 의견을 당당히 개진했어요.
examples.en: He confidently voiced his opposing view on the policy.

examples.ko: 의견을 개진하기 전에 근거부터 정리해 두세요.
examples.en: Before you state your opinion, organize your evidence first.

examples.ko: 신입 사원도 눈치 보지 않고 생각을 개진할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even new employees can voice their thoughts without worrying about others' reactions.

examples.ko: 주민들이 시청에 불만을 개진한 뒤 길이 고쳐졌어요.
examples.en: After residents voiced their complaints to city hall, the road was repaired.

examples.ko: 자기 입장만 개진하고 남의 말은 안 들으면 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you only state your own position and don't listen to others, there is no conversation.

explain: '말하다'보다 훨씬 딱딱해서 회의, 토론, 공문서 같은 격식 있는 자리에서 어울려요. 보통 '의견', '주장', '입장', '불만'과 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '의견을 내다'나 '말씀드리다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: In the debate, he clearly stated his own argument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견뿐 아니라 주장, 입장도 개진한다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides opinions, you can also state claims and positions with this verb.

phrases.en: Please feel free to give your opinion in the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개진하다보다 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase, more natural than 개진하다 in daily talk.

phrases.en: The mood was heavy, so I couldn't state my opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 못하다'를 붙여 말하고 싶었지만 못 했다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -지 못하다 it means one wanted to speak but could not.

explain_en: It is much stiffer than '말하다' and suits formal settings such as meetings, debates and official documents. It usually goes with words like '의견', '주장', '입장' and '불만'. In everyday conversation, '의견을 내다' or '말씀드리다' sounds more natural.

en: to be backed up (by evidence); to be supported

examples.en: This claim is backed up by solid data.
That theory was supported by several experiments.
If skill doesn't back it up, confidence alone is not enough.

examples.ko: 말이 행동으로 뒷받침돼야 믿을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Words can be trusted only when actions back them up.
There is not a single piece of supporting evidence.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 충분한 예산으로 뒷받침될 거예요.
examples.en: This plan will be backed by a sufficient budget.

explain: '뒷받침하다'는 받쳐 주는 쪽이고, '뒷받침되다'는 받쳐 줌을 받는 쪽이에요. 보통 '자료, 증거, 실력으로 뒷받침되다'처럼 주장이나 계획이 주어로 와요.

phrases.en: This data supports my opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷받침되다'는 받쳐 줌을 받는 쪽이고, '뒷받침하다'는 받쳐 주는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뒷받침하다' is the one that supports; '뒷받침되다' is the one that gets supported.

phrases.en: That claim isn't backed up by evidence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근거가 부족하다고 비판할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to criticize a claim for lacking evidence.

phrases.example: 이 자료는 내 주장에 큰 뒷받침이 돼요.
phrases.en: This data is a big support for my claim.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷받침되다'와 뜻이 같고, 조금 풀어서 말한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '뒷받침되다' in a slightly spelled-out form.

explain_en: '뒷받침하다' is the side that gives support, and '뒷받침되다' is the side that receives it. The subject is usually a claim or plan, as in '자료로 뒷받침되다' (backed up by data).
